summary: Accept-queue backpressure during large embedding funnel causing intermittent 5xx and upstream runtime restarts
description: Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-01 05:40 UTC EdgeLens reported a sustained elevation in 5xx responses on their dedicated embedding route under a large batching upload (embedding funnel). Impact: customer ingestion pipeline saw ~18% failed batches, downstream consumers falling behind; several upstream runtime workers restarted during the same window. Environment: dedicated tenant on prod|us-east using rw-embed-4k-v2 with batching enabled and priority routing to dedicated embedding worker pools. Steps to reproduce: 1) Submit concurrent embedding upload stream of mixed sizes (1k-4k tokens) from multiple clients to EdgeLens tenant. 2) Observe accept-queue growth on api-gateway and increased latency on embed route. 3) Watch runtime controller logs for preempt/evict events and NVML warnings. Observed behavior: api-gateway accept queue grows, connection backpressure causes hedged retries and 429/5xx amplification. Serving runtime reports KV cache lock contention and then OOM-like watchdog restarts on a subset of embedding workers. Logs/metrics (selected): - api-gateway: accept_queue_depth peaking at ~900 (normal <200), conn_accept_rate drop by 40% - runtime: kvcache_lock_waits spiking to 1200/s, worker_watchdog_restarts x6 - scheduler: preempt_eviction_count increased by 3x - customer: ingestion job failed rate ~18% during window Relevant traces/dashboards: embed-ingest-latency, accept-queue-health, runtime-watchdog. Customer notes: "We push large batched uploads every 6 hours; this first triggered during our midnight ingest window when we increased batch size."
comments: 2026-03-01 06:12 - Support (Ava): Logged initial report from EdgeLens; collected headers, sample request IDs (rids: rid_8e7b, rid_8e9c) and top-line metrics and routed to SRE.

2026-03-01 07:05 - SRE (Liam): Confirmed accept_queue_depth abnormal on prod|us-east for tenant; observed hedged retry amplification from api-gateway configs. Temporarily increased accept queue capacity on ingress to mitigate immediate failures.

2026-03-02 09:22 - Customer (EdgeLens, Jordan): Noted partial reduction after temporary mitigation but still see intermittent batch failures and occasional runtime restarts tied to large embeddings. Asked for permanent fix and rollback-safe mitigation.

2026-03-03 11:40 - Platform Eng (Rhea Singh): Proposed patch to ingress admission control to apply elastic batching windows per-tenant and throttle high-cost requests earlier in pipeline; flagged runtime kvcache path for review. Created PR referenced in ticket.

2026-03-03 14:00 - Support (Ava): Scheduled maintenance window for controlled rollout of ingress admission change and conservative kvcache backoff to avoid runtime restarts; customer notified and approved.

2026-03-03 16:10 - SRE (Liam): Ongoing monitoring post-rollout shows accept_queue_depth drop to <250 and kvcache_lock_waits reduced by ~70%. Still tracking small tail of restarts potentially due to fragmented GPU memory from older processes.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Mixed-size embedding funnel causes priority misclassification at ingress resulting in large batches occupying accept queue and forcing hedged retries that cascade into 5xx amplification.
Hypothesis 2: KVCACHE lock contention during large-embedding prefetch increases worker latencies and triggers watchdog restarts under transient memory pressure.
Evidence: correlating trace IDs show hedged retry spikes aligned with accept_queue_depth peaks. NVML logs show transient allocation failures on two workers before restart.
Dashboards used: embed-ingest-latency (panel 2), accept-queue-health, runtime-watchdog (panels 4-6). Slack thread: #support-prod (link: slack.com/archives/C0123456/p1623456789000).
Temp mitigation applied: increased ingress accept queue cap, lowered hedged-retry aggressiveness on embed route, and disabled optimistic prefetch for rw-embed-4k-v2 for the customer tenant.
Next steps: instrument per-request token cost header to ingress for better admission control; refactor kvcache lock to finer-grained sharding; schedule follow-up load test with EdgeLens dataset.
resolution: Workaround: temporary ingress accept-queue cap increase and hedged-retry tuning deployed (rolled back after controlled test window). This reduced immediate 5xx failures and prevented further runtime restarts during peak ingest.

Permanent plan: implement per-tenant admission control that applies cost-based throttling for large embedding uploads and add per-request token estimate header pipeline. Also plan kvcache lock sharding and memory-fragmentation mitigation in serving-runtime milestone M34.

Rollout notes: change to ingress admission control will be rolled out gradually across regions with canary tests; target complete in two weeks pending QA. Customer notified and agrees to staged rollout.
Follow-up actions: assign ENG-PLAT-1425 for kvcache refactor; schedule joint load test with EdgeLens in staging (owner: Solutions Eng, estimated date 2026-03-10).
